To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DEA-P was more effective than Protect-It and PyriSec on all maize hybrids in terms of mortality, progeny production and adherence to kernels.
DEA-P is more effective than Protect-It and PyriSec against P. truncatus in maize hybrids and it is also more effective than Protect-it and PyriSec in reducing progeny production.
the DE, DEA-P, is very effective in the control of the stored-product pest, P. truncatus, at low doses, and it is also able to protect maize kernels against this noxious species.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the comparison of the insecticidal effect of three DEs on five different maize varieties and it is expected to be useful in terms of the development of eco-friendly control strategies for P. truncatus in the stored-product industry.
the development of new eco-friendly approaches for the control of stored-product insects and mites.
the development of an integrated pest management (IPM) program for maize stored by smallholder farmers in tropical regions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the efficacy of DEs for the control of stored-product insects may be moderated by their application on different grain hybrids or varieties.
DEA-P is a more promising DE to be applied to different maize hybrids than Protect-It and PyriSec.
DEA-P at 75 PPM is the best DE for the control of the maize weevil, Prostephanus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the efficacy of DEs against P. truncatus is dependent on the maize hybrids they are applied to and that DEA-P at low dose is a good option to protect maize hybrids against P. truncata infestations.
the choice of the maize hybrid to be treated with DE is a crucial factor for its successful application.
the DEs tested here could be considered as a good alternative for the control of the maize infestations by P. truncatus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DEs tested in this study can be used as protectants against P. truncatus, but the DEs and the maize hybrid to be treated must be carefully considered.
the choice of DEs and maize hybrids for the control of stored-product insects and mites is crucial and needs to be taken into consideration by the stored-product entomologists.

DEs are able to successfully control P. truncatus on different maize hybrids; however, their efficacy is moderated by the maize hybrid and the DE tested, and therefore, the choice of the maize hybrid is critical for the success of DE-based control of this noxious pest.
